heroSub: 10 hand-picked budget Pattaya stays we've reviewed in depth — roomy serviced suites with a kitchenette, a highly rated design capsule hostel, a beachfront hotel a road crossing from the sand, and a budget boutique from the B2 chain near Jomtien Beach. Prices from around ฿650–1,000/night.

breadcrumbSchema.name: Top 10 Budget Stays Under ฿1,000 in Pattaya

introH2: 🏙️ How many kinds of budget stays does Pattaya have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: "A few-hundred-baht stay" in Pattaya doesn't have to mean sleeping somewhere run-down, and that's what makes choosing a budget stay here more fun than you'd expect — some are roomy serviced suites with a separate living area and a kitchenette in the room, good for longer stays and families; some are yellow-toned design capsules that are cleaner and more private than your average hostel; some are beachfront hotels where you cross the road and you're at the sea; and some are budget boutiques from the B2 chain with clean, modern-looking rooms that punch above their price. A lot of people assume paying less means trading down to grime or a far-flung location, and end up missing good stays hiding in the same budget. This article rounds up 10 budget Pattaya stays we've reviewed in depth, across Central Pattaya, South Pattaya, Pratamnak, Jomtien and Na Jomtien — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you the upsides and the honest caveats alike, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links for all of them.
mrtHtml: Pattaya has no metro, but getting around town is easy with the songthaew (baht bus) that loops the city all day starting at a few baht, or you can hail a Grab or a motorbike taxi. From Bangkok it's about a 1.5–2 hour drive on the motorway; from U-Tapao Airport (UTP) it's about 35–45 min into town. The areas in this article: Central Pattaya — the city centre, walk to the beach, Terminal 21 and the Alcazar show · South Pattaya / Beach Road — near Walking Street and the nightlife, beachfront rooms a road crossing from the sea · Pratamnak — where the city meets Pratamnak Hill, quieter but still walkable down into town · Jomtien / Na Jomtien — the quieter seaside zone, good if you have a car and want a relaxed stay.

toc.name: The Grass Serviced Suites by At Mind

entries.name: The Grass Serviced Suites by At Mind
entries.badge: 🏆 Highest score · roomy with a kitchenette
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Pattaya·South Pattaya Rd · ~10 min drive to the beach
tags: 🛋️ All-suite with a separate living area
entries.addr: 554, 599/9 Moo 10, South Pattaya Road, Nongprue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: Among the budget Pattaya stays we've reviewed, on score alone The Grass Serviced Suites by At Mind is the highest-rated in this article at 9.4, from as many as 3,355 reviews on Trip.com · It's a 4-star serviced apartment in the At Mind group set on South Pattaya Road in Central Pattaya, opened in 2016 and freshly renovated in 2024 · What makes a lot of people fall for it and mention it again and again in reviews is that every room is an all-suite with a separate living area and its own kitchenette — a big fridge, a microwave, a kettle and a dining nook, giving you space more like a private condo than a square hotel box · Even the entry-level Deluxe at around 26 sqm clearly splits the living zone from the sleeping zone, and there's a Two Bedroom Bunk Bed family room at around 42 sqm with bunk beds the kids will love · There's an outdoor pool, a gym, a sauna, a massage spa, a garden cafe and free parking · Real reviews line up that it's best for families travelling with kids, people staying several nights, and anyone who wants a kitchen to cook in and save on food · The honest caveats from the reviews: it's not on the beach, so you take a red songthaew or drive about 10 minutes out to Pattaya Beach and Walking Street; the wings that haven't been renovated yet are older than the updated rooms; there are reports of cigarette smell in some rooms and the odd small insect at times; and check-in is sometimes later than 14:00 when it's busy · This isn't the seafront option, but it's the best value for usable space in the few-hundred-baht budget, especially for families and longer stays.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a 2024-renovated, non-smoking room at the time of booking · And if you're staying a while, make the most of the in-room kitchen — buy from a nearby minimart and cook your own meals to save a lot on food.
pros: Highest score in the article, 9.4 from 3,355 reviews · roomy rooms with a kitchenette throughout
All-suite with a separate living area, 26–42 sqm, spacious like a private condo
Pool, gym, sauna, spa and free parking · renovated 2024
Good for families and longer stays, the kitchen helps save on food (from the reviews)
cons: Not on the beach, you take a red songthaew or drive to Walking Street and Pattaya Beach
Some unrenovated wings are older than the updated rooms · reports of cigarette smell in some rooms
Check-in is sometimes later than 14:00 when it's busy (from the reviews)

entries.name: A-One Star Hotel Pattaya
entries.badge: 🏖️ Most reviewed · a road crossing to the beach
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Beach Road·Central Pattaya · ~30 m across the road to the beach
tags: 🏖️ A road crossing to Pattaya Beach
entries.addr: 115/11 Moo 9 Pattaya Beach Road, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: Among the budget Pattaya stays, on review count alone A-One Star Hotel Pattaya is the most reviewed in this article by a wide margin — as many as 16,533 reviews on Agoda, an overall score around 8.3 that climbs to about 8.7 in the post-renovation reviews · It's a 258-room 3-star hotel planted on Beach Road in Central Pattaya, opened in 2013 and renovated in 2023 · An important detail many people don't know: the hotel has rebranded as Mood Hotel Pattaya — if you search A-One Star and find Mood Hotel on some platforms, no doubt about it, it's the same place, same building, same location, same address at 115/11 Moo 9 (don't confuse it with A-One The Royal Cruise, which is a different hotel) · The number-one selling point reviews agree on is the location — cross the road and you're at Pattaya Beach, only about 30 metres from the sand, a 5–10 minute walk to Terminal 21 Pattaya, and a quick ride on to Walking Street and Bali Hai Pier for boats to Koh Larn · There's an outdoor rooftop pool looking over Pattaya Bay, a popular spot to chill and watch the sunset in the evening, and you can use some of the spa and pool facilities shared with the adjacent A-One The Royal Cruise · The honest caveats from the reviews: because it's a 2013 building that's only been partly renovated, room quality is inconsistent — rooms that haven't been updated can look dated or have a musty smell from the air-con; the Beach Road area buzzes all night, so rooms facing the road or on lower floors hear traffic and nightlife into the small hours; and service at peak times is inconsistent because it's a big hotel with high turnover · It's best for anyone who wants to stay by the central beach on an affordable budget and plans to use the hotel as a base to hit the beach, shop and eat street food every day.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a renovated, high-floor, sea-facing room at the time of booking to escape the road noise and get a Pattaya Bay view · And pack earplugs just in case, since this area buzzes into the small hours.
pros: Most reviewed in the article, 16,533 reviews · beachfront location, a road crossing to the sea
Rooftop pool with a Pattaya Bay view, shared spa/pool with A-One The Royal Cruise
Walk to Terminal 21 and Central · affordable for a beachfront location
Rooms renovated after 2023 are cleaner and brighter (from the reviews)
cons: 2013 building, partly renovated, inconsistent room quality, some rooms are musty
On the lively Beach Road, road-facing rooms hear noise into the small hours
Big 258-room hotel, inconsistent service at peak times, some queueing (from the reviews)

entries.name: Nonze Hostel
entries.badge: 🛏️ Highly rated capsules · cheapest in the group
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Beach Road·South Pattaya · 7 min walk to Walking Street
tags: 🛏️ Capsules with a private sliding door
🌇 Rooftop with a Pattaya Bay view
entries.addr: 183/6 Beach Road, Moo 10, Nongprue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If you think a hostel has to be cramped and noisy, Nonze Hostel will change your mind — and it's the cheapest starting price in this article at around ฿700/night · It's a bright yellow-toned design capsule hostel on Beach Road in the southern part of Pattaya, opened in 2016, with a high 9.2 score from several thousand real reviews, which is very high for a hostel · What sets it apart from your usual bunk-bed dorm is that every air-conditioned capsule has a sliding door that closes for privacy, lockable from the inside, with a reading light, a power outlet, a shelf and a coat hook, and everyone gets a keycard-operated locker · There are several capsule types, from the mixed dorm up to a Capsule Suite in 2-, 4- and 8-unit setups for groups of friends who want to share a room · The highlight of the common areas is the rooftop looking out over Pattaya Bay, a popular spot to sip a coffee and watch the sunset, alongside a bar, a billiards room and freebies like coffee and towels that many hostels charge extra for · It's a 7-minute walk to Walking Street, near Royal Garden Plaza, Ripley's and Bali Hai Pier — foreign reviews rate the location category as high as about 9.7 · Real reviews say it's best for solo travellers, couples, or groups of friends on a budget who want a clean capsule in a central location · The honest caveats: being near Walking Street, road noise and guests in the common areas can get loud late at night; the capsule light isn't bright enough to read by for long; every capsule uses shared bathrooms, none en-suite; and the laundry-drying space is limited · It's not for you if you need a private room with an en-suite bathroom or you're travelling with young kids, but if you just use the stay to sleep and head out all day, this is the best value in the low few-hundred-baht budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Bring earplugs and ask for a capsule away from the bar or lounge at check-in for a quieter night · And head up to the rooftop in the evening for the Pattaya Bay view at sunset, with free coffee.
pros: Cheapest in the article, from around ฿700/night · 9.2 score from several thousand reviews
Capsules with a private sliding door, keycard lockers, cleaner and more private than a usual dorm
Rooftop with a Pattaya Bay view · free coffee and towels · 7 min walk to Walking Street
Friendly staff, help booking Koh Larn tours and hailing rides (from the reviews)
cons: Capsules in a dorm with shared bathrooms, not for anyone who needs a completely quiet private room
Near Walking Street, road noise and guests can get loud late · limited laundry-drying space
The capsule light isn't bright enough to read by for long (from the reviews)

entries.name: Manita Boutique Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pratamnak·South Pattaya · 10–15 min walk to Walking Street
entries.storyHtml: Picture a small hotel with a garden pool you can use day and night, in an area a few minutes' walk from Walking Street, but with a starting price still in the high few hundreds — Manita Boutique Hotel is a 3-star boutique in the Pratamnak/South Pattaya area that's been open since 2008 and is still a budget favourite today, with an 8.5 score from 1,320 reviews on Trip.com · The most talked-about feature in reviews is the outdoor garden pool open 24 hours, ringed with trees for a shady, private feel — a lot of people love that they can come back from a late night out and still take a cooling dip, which is rare at this price · There are 82 studio-style rooms, from the cheapest Superior up to the King Room with Balcony with its own balcony, and every room has air-con, a fridge, a minibar and free Wi-Fi · Beyond the pool there's a massage room, a restaurant and bar with a good-value happy hour, a 24-hour reception, and free private parking · The Pratamnak location is a short walk or songthaew ride to Walking Street in about 10–15 minutes, Pattaya Beach is about 1.7 km away and Jomtien Beach about 3 km · Service is a strength reviews praise often, with several mentions of free room upgrades and helpful staff · The honest caveats from the reviews: the hotel sits on a busy main road, so rooms facing the road or on the lower floors hear traffic clearly; the building and rooms are starting to show their age since it opened in 2008, with paint peeling in spots; some ground-floor rooms have damp or a musty smell; the breakfast menu is still limited; and there's no convenience store right at the door · It's best for budget travellers who want a central location in the tourist district, a pool to use all day, and money left over to make the most of their trip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a high-floor inner room that doesn't face the road, and pack earplugs since the hotel is on a main road · Make the most of the 24-hour pool, and bring your own water and essentials since there's no convenience store right at the door.
pros: Outdoor pool open 24 hours, usable day and night, rare at this price
Good value in the budget group, with a pool, free parking and a massage room
Pratamnak location, walk to Walking Street and Pattaya Beach, songthaews pass all the time
Friendly staff, occasional room upgrades (from the reviews)
cons: On a busy main road, traffic noise in rooms facing the road or on lower floors
Building opened in 2008, rooms show their age, some ground-floor rooms have damp or a musty smell
Limited breakfast menu · no convenience store right at the door (from the reviews)

entries.name: B2 Hotel South Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 South Pattaya · 15–20 min walk to Walking Street
entries.addr: 321/9 Moo 10, South Pattaya Road, Nongprue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If you come to Pattaya not wanting to spend on a pricey room, preferring to save your money for eating, going out and walking Walking Street rather than just sitting in the room, B2 Hotel South Pattaya — or B2 South Pattaya as Thais call it — is a name a lot of people pick · It's a budget boutique in the B2 Hotel chain, a Thai brand with a clear stance of "pay less, but get a clean, good-looking room," with a 7.5 score from 1,531 reviews on Trip.com · The B2 brand's signature is its grey-and-black decor that looks more modern than the price suggests, so even though it's a budget hotel, you walk in and don't feel like you're staying somewhere cheap · The 84-room building in South Pattaya has rooms from the compact Superior up to the Deluxe Triple for three, and every room has air-con, a flat-screen TV, a small fridge, free drinking water and free Wi-Fi · There's a decent-sized outdoor pool, a small gym, a 24-hour front desk, and a feature reviewers who drive love most — free parking, which is hard to find in Pattaya · The South Pattaya location is about a 15–20 minute walk to the mouth of Walking Street, or a quick ride, and there are restaurants and a convenience store within walking distance · Real reviews say it's best for budget travellers, couples on a short trip, groups of friends out for the nightlife, and self-drivers who want free parking · The honest caveats: some rooms are fairly small with no special view; breakfast is plain with limited choice; staff service is inconsistent at times; the South Pattaya area is lively at night so road-facing rooms hear some noise; and if you're not driving, getting around relies on the songthaew or Grab · Be careful not to book the wrong branch, since B2 has several in Pattaya — check that it's the South Pattaya one.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want more space, choose the Deluxe Premier or Triple and specify it at booking · Ask for a non-road-facing room if you're a light sleeper, and if you're driving, make the most of the free parking — ask about availability ahead when the hotel is full.
pros: Very affordable in the South Pattaya area, clean rooms and comfortable bedding
Modern grey-and-black decor, looks better than the price · the familiar B2 chain
Free parking, hard to find in Pattaya · an outdoor pool and free Wi-Fi
Location near Walking Street and restaurants around the hotel (from the reviews)
cons: Some rooms are fairly small with no special view · limited breakfast choice
Staff service is inconsistent at times
If you're not driving, getting around relies on the songthaew or Grab (from the reviews)

entries.name: Red Planet Pattaya
entries.badge: 🚶 5 min walk to the beach · city centre
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Pattaya·Pattaya 2nd Road · 5 min walk to the beach
entries.addr: 255/7 Pattaya Sai Song Rd (Pattaya 2nd Road), Central Pattaya, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If your Pattaya trip is planned around spending most of your time out — walking around, eating well, catching a show — then coming back to sleep comfortably on a budget that doesn't blow out, Red Planet Pattaya is a name budget travellers have talked about for a long time, with an 8.0 score from over 3,200 reviews combined · It's a 192-room 3-star budget hotel on Pattaya 2nd Road near Soi 13, in the heart of Central Pattaya · An important thing to understand before booking: this hotel has changed names several times — it was originally the Tune Hotel brand, then Red Planet, and now goes by Easy Planet Pattaya on many booking platforms — same building, same location, so if you can't find Red Planet, try the new name or look it up by address · The three things real reviews praise most consistently are clean rooms, firm comfortable beds, and ice-cold air-con, the three things budget travellers care about most · Location is the main selling point — about a 5-minute walk to Pattaya's beach road, about a 10–11 minute walk to Terminal 21, and near the Alcazar show, The Avenue and Central Marina · There's a 24-hour reception, luggage storage, smooth free Wi-Fi, and free parking, which is rare in a city-centre location · The honest thing to say straight: there's no pool and no gym here — it's a budget hotel focused purely on a place to sleep; rooms are fairly small and some have no window; cleanliness is inconsistent in spots so check the room at check-in; and the Central Pattaya area buzzes all night · It's best for travellers who use the hotel as a base to go out, eat and catch a show, and just want a good place to sleep near everything at a price that doesn't blow out.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The hotel now goes by Easy Planet Pattaya on many platforms, so if you can't find it, try the new name · Specify a room with a window if light and airflow matter to you, and ask for a high-floor room on the side away from Pattaya 2nd Road if you're a light sleeper.
pros: Heart-of-Central-Pattaya location, 5 min walk to the beach, walk to Terminal 21 and the Alcazar
Genuinely cheap, clean rooms, firm comfortable beds, cold air-con
24-hour reception, luggage storage · free parking · good Wi-Fi
Plenty of restaurants and convenience stores around the hotel (from the reviews)
cons: No pool and no gym, a budget hotel focused purely on a place to sleep
Rooms are fairly small, some have no window · cleanliness is inconsistent in spots
The area buzzes all night, road-facing rooms hear noise from the street (from the reviews)

entries.name: Diamond City Place Hotel Pattaya
entries.badge: 🍳 Rooms with a kitchenette · near Walking Street
entries.mrtTag: 📍 South Pattaya Road · 10–15 min walk to Walking Street
entries.addr: 513 Moo 10, South Pattaya Road, Nongprue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If you're hunting for a light-on-the-wallet Pattaya stay with roomy rooms that you can walk from out into South Pattaya without taking a ride, Diamond City Place Hotel is a name that comes up often in both Thai and foreign reviews, with real scores around 7.8–8.3 from thousands of guests on Agoda and Trip.com · It's an older-style 3-star hotel of about 60 rooms on South Pattaya Road that sells a walk-to-everything location, roomy rooms and a genuinely affordable price · What sets it apart from same-priced hotels is that many room types are roomier than you'd expect and come with a kitchenette and a fridge, some with a separate seating area and a private balcony, so people staying several nights can buy from the convenience store and cook for themselves to save on food · There's an outdoor pool with a separate kids' pool that families with little ones like, and free on-site parking that's rare in the South Pattaya area · Another highlight is that it's a guest-friendly hotel with no joiner fee · The location is about a 10–15 minute walk to Walking Street, Ripley's, Louis Tussaud's and Pattaya Beach, with songthaews running past the front all the time · Real reviews say it's best for nightlife travellers who want to walk back to the hotel, groups of friends who want a roomy room to share, and families who want a kids' pool · The honest caveats: the building and furniture are starting to show their age, it's not a new build; the pool is small and closes fairly early at around 8 pm; Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms; breakfast choice is limited; service is inconsistent at times; and road-facing rooms hear the pubs and discos on Friday and Saturday nights.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're staying a while, choose a room with a kitchenette to save a lot on food · Ask for a room not facing the main road and ask about recently updated rooms at booking · And if you plan to use the pool, go midday to evening since it closes around 8 pm.
pros: Rooms roomier than the price, many with a kitchenette and a fridge, you can cook for yourself
10–15 min walk to Walking Street, Ripley's and Pattaya Beach
Free on-site parking · a kids' pool for families · guest-friendly
Affordable value, many staff are friendly (from the reviews)
cons: The building and furniture are starting to show their age · Wi-Fi is weak in some rooms
The pool is small and closes fairly early at around 8 pm
Limited breakfast choice · road-facing rooms hear noise on weekend nights (from the reviews)

entries.name: B2 Sea View Pattaya Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Jomtien Soi 14 · ~1 km to Na Jomtien Beach
tags: 🌊 Rooms with a Jomtien bay view
entries.addr: 19/22 Moo 2, Soi Na Jomtien 14, Na Jomtien, Sattahip
entries.storyHtml: Picture waking up, opening the curtains and finding a wide view of Jomtien Bay from your own balcony, while paying only high few hundreds to low thousands for the room — B2 Sea View Pattaya Hotel, B2 Sea View Pattaya as Thais call it, plays the "budget sea view" card pretty well, with an 8.1 score from 538 reviews on Trip.com · It's a budget boutique in the B2 chain, and what sets this branch apart is the Na Jomtien location, quieter than Central Pattaya, with many rooms that have a balcony looking out to the sea · The rooms here are noticeably roomier than the budget-hotel average, from the Superior Premier Garden View at around 30 sqm up to the highlight Luxury Premier Sea View at around 42 sqm, a king-bed room with a sea-view balcony that reviews mention and recommend most · The decor is the B2 brand's signature modern exposed-concrete grey-and-black look, raw and stylishly modern · There's roomy free parking, free Wi-Fi, a lift, CCTV and a 24-hour front desk · Real reviews say it's best for people with their own car, couples who want a quiet stay near the sea, and anyone who wants to avoid the bustle of Central Pattaya · The honest caveat to understand before booking: the name "Pattaya" can mislead — this is about 1 km from Na Jomtien Beach and about 15–20 minutes by car from Central Pattaya, so getting around is hard without your own car since public transport around the hotel is scarce · The pool is a small indoor one that's dark with cold water, which many barely use and which draws the most criticism in reviews; breakfast choice is limited and the restaurants nearby open late; and a minority of reviews mention insects in the room and nearby construction noise · Be careful not to book the wrong branch, since B2 has several — check that it's the Sea View one.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The real selling point is the sea view, so ask for a high-floor Luxury Premier Sea View room at booking — don't book a Garden View room and expect a sea view · And this place suits people with a car, so if you don't have one, plan to rent a motorbike.
pros: Rooms roomier than the price, many with a Jomtien-bay-view balcony
Modern exposed-concrete grey-and-black decor, looks better than the price · clean rooms, comfy beds
The Na Jomtien area is quiet and relaxing, good for a getaway
Roomy free parking, good for self-drivers (from the reviews)
cons: About 1 km from the beach and far from Central Pattaya, you need a car, little public transport
The indoor pool is small, dark and cold, many barely use it
Limited breakfast choice, restaurants nearby open late (from the reviews)

entries.name: LK Mansion
entries.badge: 🛏️ Roomy rooms with a fridge · central Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Pattaya Road · ~800 m walk to Pattaya Beach
tags: 📍 Walk to the beach and Central
entries.addr: 341/38 Moo 9, Central Pattaya Road, Nongprue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If you're looking for a central Pattaya stay that's light on the wallet, with roomy rooms and a walk to the beach and the night market, without paying resort-by-the-sea prices, LK Mansion in the LK Group on Central Pattaya Road is one name frequent Pattaya visitors talk about, with review scores around 7.6 from thousands of real guests · It's a 3-star apart-hotel in the LK Group, a big local accommodation group in Pattaya with many properties across the city, so frequent Pattaya visitors know the group's name well · LK Mansion sits in the budget tier, and its selling point is apart-hotel-style rooms roomier than the price, with a fridge and good usable space, from Standard up to Studio and Deluxe getting progressively bigger, good for groups of friends and families who need space · There's a rooftop pool, an in-building restaurant and bar, a 24-hour front desk, and parking · The standout of the location is "close to but set back from the Beach Road noise" — about an 800-metre walk to Pattaya Beach, Central Pattaya mall a short walk away, and the Alcazar show about 1.1 km off · Real reviews say it's best for budget travellers, couples, groups of friends, and families who want suite-style rooms with a fridge and a central location · The honest caveat to say straight: it's an older building that's only been partly renovated, so room quality is fairly inconsistent — some older rooms have furniture starting to show wear, and some people call the rooms run-down; reviews mention water problems at times, like weak flow, temporary outages or cloudy water; air-con in some rooms doesn't get fully cold or is noisy; Wi-Fi is slow in some rooms; and there's some outside noise on weekend nights · The key tip from many guests is to ask for a room in a renovated wing at the time of booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The hotel has both old and new rooms and the quality is inconsistent, so ask for a room in a renovated wing at the time of booking, and if you get a room you don't like, ask the 24-hour front desk to change it · Bring a mobile SIM as backup since Wi-Fi is slow in some rooms.
pros: Apart-hotel-style rooms roomier than the price, with a fridge, good for groups and families
Central Pattaya location, ~800 m walk to the beach, near Central and the Alcazar
Close to but set back from the Beach Road noise · a rooftop pool and parking
Rooms in the renovated wing are clean and pleasant · friendly staff (from the reviews)
cons: Inconsistent room quality, some older rooms look run-down
Reviews mention water problems at times (weak flow/outage/cloudy)
Air-con in some rooms doesn't get fully cold or is noisy · Wi-Fi is slow in some rooms (from the reviews)

entries.name: B2 Jomtien Pattaya
entries.badge: 🏖️ Walk to Jomtien Beach · cheapest from ฿650
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Jomtien·Na Jomtien · ~700 m walk to the beach
entries.storyHtml: If you come to Pattaya and want to stay somewhere quieter than Central Pattaya, near the sea within walking distance, but don't want to pay a high room rate, B2 Jomtien Pattaya Boutique & Budget Hotel — B2 Jomtien for short among Thais — is a name a lot of people pick, and it's the cheapest starting price in this article at around ฿650/night · It's a budget boutique in the B2 Hotel chain, known for clean, modern rooms at a light price, with an 8.3 score from 534 reviews on Trip.com · The B2 brand's signature is its grey-and-black decor that looks more modern than the price suggests, so you walk in and don't feel like you're staying somewhere cheap · The 80-room building in Jomtien has rooms from the Superior at around 24 sqm up to the Luxury Garden View at around 30 sqm, roomier with an easy-on-the-eye garden view, and every room has air-con, a flat-screen TV, a small fridge, free drinking water and free Wi-Fi · There's an in-building cafe called Copper Cafe, free parking, a lift and a 24-hour front desk · The standout of the location is being in the Jomtien area, which many credit with a prettier, quieter sea than the Central Pattaya side — about a 700-metre walk to Jomtien Beach, about a 10-minute drive to Walking Street, and with plenty of seafront seafood restaurants around the hotel · Real reviews say it's best for budget travellers, couples on a short trip, small families who want to be near Jomtien Beach, and self-drivers who want free parking · The honest caveat to make clear so there's no confusion: this Jomtien branch has no pool (a different branch from B2 Sea View) — if you're coming to swim at the hotel, this isn't the option, but Jomtien Beach is only about 700 metres away, an easy walk to swim in the actual sea · Some rooms are fairly compact; breakfast isn't a big buffet and some packages don't include it; some long-closed rooms have a musty smell; and parts of the area still have construction sites that can be noisy during the day · Double-check you've booked the right branch, since B2 has several in Pattaya.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Double-check you've booked B2 Jomtien and understand this branch has no pool · If you want more space, choose the Deluxe Premier or Luxury Garden View · And head out for seafood and street food along Jomtien Beach since the breakfast choice is limited.
pros: Cheapest starting price in the article, around ฿650/night · clean rooms, comfortable bedding
Modern grey-and-black decor, looks better than the price · the familiar B2 chain
About a 700 m walk to Jomtien Beach · quieter than Central Pattaya, restful sleep
Free parking · in-building cafe · 24-hour front desk (from the reviews)
cons: No pool (a different branch from B2 Sea View), you walk to the beach to swim
Some rooms are fairly compact · breakfast isn't a big buffet, some packages don't include it
Parts of the area still have construction that can be noisy during the day (from the reviews)

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard-room range on weekdays and may change by day and season — we recommend checking the real price and comparing the 3 sites before every booking · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms; we did not stay ourselves · Some hotels have changed names — A-One Star Hotel rebranded as Mood Hotel Pattaya, and Red Planet now goes by Easy Planet Pattaya (the same place, same building, same location) · The B2 chain has several branches in Pattaya (South Pattaya/Jomtien/Na Jomtien), so check you're booking the branch you want · Over long weekends, Songkran and the high season (Nov–Feb), prices rise and rooms sell out fast, so book ahead · Pattaya has no metro — the songthaew, Grab or a motorbike taxi are convenient, and it's about 35–45 min from U-Tapao Airport into town · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about budget stays in Pattaya

faq.q: ❓ What's the best budget stay in Pattaya?
faq.a: It depends on your style of trip · On score, The Grass Serviced Suites has the highest at 9.4 in the article, with roomy kitchenette rooms throughout · On review count, A-One Star Hotel is the most reviewed at over 16,000, with a beachfront location · On the tightest budget for a clean sleep, Nonze Hostel capsules at 9.2 or B2 Jomtien from ฿650, the cheapest · For a pool on a light budget, Manita Boutique with a pool open 24 hours

faq.q: ❓ How much does a few-hundred-baht stay in Pattaya cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at around ฿650–1,000 per night on weekdays · The cheapest is B2 Jomtien from ฿650 · In the ฿700 group are Nonze Hostel, B2 South Pattaya, Red Planet and Diamond City Place · B2 Sea View starts at ฿750 · The Grass, Manita and LK Mansion start at ฿900 · A-One Star starts at ฿1,000 · All prices are approximate starting rates from a standard room, and they climb fast over weekends and the high season

faq.q: ❓ Which area should you stay in if you're on a budget in Pattaya?
faq.a: Central Pattaya suits people who want to be in the city centre, walking to the beach and the malls (The Grass, A-One Star, Red Planet, LK Mansion) · South Pattaya/Beach Road suits people who like the nightlife, a walk to Walking Street (Nonze, B2 South Pattaya, Diamond City Place) · Pratamnak is a quieter edge of the city (Manita) · Jomtien/Na Jomtien suits people with a car who want to relax near a quiet sea (B2 Sea View, B2 Jomtien)

faq.q: ❓ Are A-One Star and Mood Hotel · Red Planet and Easy Planet the same place?
faq.a: Yes, both · A-One Star Hotel was renovated in 2023 and rebranded as Mood Hotel Pattaya, the same building and address (115/11 Moo 9 Pattaya Beach Road) — don't confuse it with A-One The Royal Cruise, which is a different hotel · And Red Planet was originally Tune Hotel and now goes by Easy Planet Pattaya, the same building and location on Pattaya 2nd Road · If you can't find the old name, try the new one or look it up by address

faq.q: ❓ Which budget stays in Pattaya have a pool?
faq.a: Manita Boutique has a pool open 24 hours · The Grass has a pool, gym and sauna · A-One Star has a rooftop pool with a sea view · B2 South Pattaya and Diamond City Place (with a kids' pool) have outdoor pools · LK Mansion has a rooftop pool · B2 Sea View has a (small) indoor pool · while Red Planet, Nonze Hostel and B2 Jomtien have no pool — Nonze has a rooftop with a bay view, and B2 Jomtien is within walking distance of the beach

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a stay in Pattaya?
faq.a: Budget stays in Pattaya swing in price by day quite clearly — on Saturdays and Sundays, long weekends, and during the high season (November–February) and Songkran, prices rise and rooms sell out fast, so book 2–4 weeks ahead or more · On off-season weekdays you can book just a few days out and still get the best starting price · Every platform offers Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a rate like that first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
